name: add-key-nonallowlisted
why: a single add_key() from a process outside the keyring allowlist is the anchor the rule fires on
source: synthetic: shape of normalize() output for keyring_stuffing_behavioral.c's add_key(type, desc, payload, plen=7, KEY_SPEC_PROCESS_KEYRING) record. auditd logs a0..a3 (type/desc/payload ptrs, plen); the target keyring is a4 and is not in a0..a3. exit is the decimal key serial, not hex

name: add-key-burst
why: a rapid burst of add_key() from one non-allowlisted pid (the keyring-stuffing primitive); each call independently satisfies the rule
source: recorded: strace of keyring_stuffing_behavioral.c -- three add_key records with decimal key-serial exits and a3=plen(7)

name: keyctl-clear-not-add-key
why: keyctl() reads/updates existing keys and is far more common than add_key; it keeps the keyring-syscall surface, so the syscall==add_key anchor must be load-bearing (the atomic itself issues keyctl(KEYCTL_CLEAR, KEY_SPEC_PROCESS_KEYRING) for cleanup)
source: recorded: strace of keyring_stuffing_behavioral.c cleanup -- keyctl(KEYCTL_CLEAR=7, KEY_SPEC_PROCESS_KEYRING=0xfffffffe)

name: keyctl-join-session-not-add-key
why: keyctl(KEYCTL_JOIN_SESSION_KEYRING) is what a login/PAM path runs to set up a session keyring; same keyring surface, different syscall, so it must not fire. This replaces a prior request_key near-miss: request_key is NOT in detections/audit/atomic.rules and can never reach this pipeline, whereas keyctl is audited
source: synthetic: keyctl(KEYCTL_JOIN_SESSION_KEYRING=1) from a non-allowlisted process; keyctl is audited, request_key is not

name: systemd-allowlisted
why: systemd adds a 'user' key (invocation_id) to the session keyring for every unit it starts with a KeyringMode; the comm allowlist alone must suppress it
source: recorded via source: systemd src/core/exec-invoke.c:3403 add_key("user", "invocation_id", ...) in setup_keyring(); comm 'systemd'

name: gssproxy-allowlisted
why: gssproxy installs Kerberos credentials into the keyring via libkrb5's KEYRING ccache (add_key); the allowlisted GSSAPI identity must be filtered
source: recorded via source: krb5 lib/krb5/ccache/cc_keyring.c:713 add_key(cred key type, ...); libkrb5 is the add_key path for gssproxy/rpc.gssd

name: unrelated-write
why: an ordinary ioctl(fd, TCGETS) by a routine process: an audited syscall (atomic.rules records ioctl) that shares neither the anchored syscall nor its arguments -- a sanity floor that must stay quiet
source: synthetic: a routine ioctl(TCGETS), an audited high-volume syscall used as a non-firing floor

name: cryptsetup-luks2-volume-key-filtered
why: cryptsetup open hands the LUKS2 volume key to dm-crypt with add_key("logon", ...); the cryptsetup entry of luks_images suppresses it (the old rule fired on it). It runs as root (`sudo cryptsetup open`: uid and euid 0, auid the admin's login uid 1000), which the entry's euid condition requires
source: cryptsetup lib/utils_keyring.c (syscall(__NR_add_key, type, ...), key type "logon"); events as in the benign corpus cryptsetup template

name: systemd-cryptsetup-boot-unlock-filtered
why: systemd-cryptsetup unlocks a LUKS2 volume at boot through libcryptsetup and adds the volume key as a logon key; comm is the 15-character truncation systemd-cryptse. The systemd-cryptsetup entry of luks_images suppresses it. systemd starts it from systemd-cryptsetup@.service as root (uid and euid 0) with no login uid (auid 4294967295, unset), which the entry's euid condition requires
source: systemd src/cryptsetup (links libcryptsetup); systemd v256 src/cryptsetup/meson.build installs it public in bindir with a link in libexecdir

name: cryptsetup-comm-from-tmp
why: a stuffer that names itself cryptsetup with prctl still fires: the cryptsetup entry needs the cryptsetup binary as well as the comm

name: ldpreload-into-cryptsetup-known-miss
why: NOW CAUGHT (formerly a KNOWN MISS labelled filtered, breaks luks_images[0].exe, when the event schema had no uid): an unprivileged user runs /usr/sbin/cryptsetup, a non-setuid, dynamically linked binary, with LD_PRELOAD, and the injected code calls add_key in a loop. Each call keeps comm cryptsetup and exe /usr/sbin/cryptsetup, but carries the user's uid and euid (1000; cryptsetup is not setuid, so euid = uid). The luks_images entry requires euid 0, which every LUKS unlock has (the unlock drives device-mapper, which needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN), so this fires. It is not told apart from cryptsetup's own unprivileged add_key (--test-passphrase --link-vk-to-keyring, see cryptsetup-test-passphrase-link-vk-as-user-fires), which fires too. The same injection by a process that already runs as root is still suppressed
source: synthetic from recorded mechanism: LD_PRELOAD into a non-setuid binary keeps its comm and exe (recorded on this host for /usr/bin/gdb and /usr/bin/runc as uid 65534); event shape as cryptsetup-luks2-volume-key-filtered with the uid and auid of an unprivileged user; euid added (equal to uid: cryptsetup is not setuid, so exec does not change the euid)

name: ldpreload-into-systemd-cryptsetup-as-user
why: systemd >= 256 installs systemd-cryptsetup world-executable in /usr/bin; an unprivileged user runs it with LD_PRELOAD and the injected add_key keeps comm systemd-cryptse and its exe, but carries the user's euid, so the systemd-cryptsetup entry (euid 0) does not suppress it. The rule without the euid condition suppressed this
source: synthetic from recorded mechanism: LD_PRELOAD into a non-setuid binary keeps its comm and exe (recorded for /usr/bin/gdb and /usr/bin/runc as uid 65534, see ldpreload-into-runc-as-exe-known-miss in T1620); systemd v256 src/cryptsetup/meson.build (public in bindir); uid/euid/auid as auditd logs them for a user's login session

name: cryptsetup-root-unlock-euid-filtered
why: `sudo cryptsetup open` of a LUKS2 volume, cryptsetup at /sbin/cryptsetup (its path on a distribution without merged /usr; the kernel logs the resolved path, so a merged-/usr host logs /usr/sbin): euid 0 is what the cryptsetup entry needs beyond comm and exe, and the same event with an unprivileged euid fires (see ldpreload-into-cryptsetup-known-miss), so the euid item is load-bearing
source: cryptsetup lib/setup.c (an unlock loads the volume key into the keyring and then creates or resumes the dm-crypt device, `if (name) LUKS2_activate(...)`); linux drivers/md/dm-ioctl.c ctl_ioctl() (CAP_SYS_ADMIN for every device-mapper ioctl); kernel/audit.c audit_log_task_info() (auid, uid, euid as %u in the initial user namespace). Not every cryptsetup add_key is an unlock: with --test-passphrase --link-vk-to-keyring (cryptsetup >= 2.7.1) the key is loaded with no device name and no root, see cryptsetup-test-passphrase-link-vk-as-user-fires

name: systemd-cryptsetup-root-unlock-euid-filtered
why: systemd >= 256 runs /usr/bin/systemd-cryptsetup from systemd-cryptsetup@.service as root with no login uid; euid 0 is what the systemd-cryptsetup entry needs beyond comm and exe, and the same event with an unprivileged euid fires (see ldpreload-into-systemd-cryptsetup-as-user)
source: systemd v256 src/cryptsetup/meson.build (public in bindir) and units/systemd-cryptsetup@.service generated by systemd-cryptsetup-generator (no User=); auid 4294967295 is the unset login uid of a system service

name: cryptsetup-test-passphrase-link-vk-as-user-fires
why: DOCUMENTED FALSE POSITIVE, labelled positive because the rule fires on it (confounder and benign assert no match): a user runs `cryptsetup open --test-passphrase --link-vk-to-keyring @u::%user:vk disk.img` (cryptsetup >= 2.7.1) on a LUKS2 image the user can read. src/utils_luks.c sets CRYPT_ACTIVATE_KEYRING_KEY for --link-vk-to-keyring, lib/setup.c then loads the volume key as a "logon" key into the thread keyring and links it as the requested key, and with --test-passphrase there is no device name, so it never reaches device-mapper and needs no root. Both add_key calls carry the user's euid, so the cryptsetup entry (euid 0) does not suppress them and the rule fires twice. The falsepositives list it
source: recorded: libcryptsetup driven as euid 65534 the way `cryptsetup open --test-passphrase --link-vk-to-keyring` drives it (crypt_set_keyring_to_link("vk", "user", "@u"), crypt_activate_by_passphrase(name=NULL, CRYPT_ACTIVATE_KEYRING_KEY)); strace: add_key("logon", "cryptsetup:<uuid>...", <64-byte key>, 64, KEY_SPEC_THREAD_KEYRING) = 655398415, add_key("user", "vk", <key>, 64, KEY_SPEC_USER_KEYRING) = 126983824, no device-mapper ioctl. comm and exe here are the cryptsetup CLI's (the recording ran libcryptsetup from python3); uid/euid/auid of a login session. cryptsetup v2.7.0 lib/setup.c (use_keyring = (name && ...) || (flags & CRYPT_ACTIVATE_KEYRING_KEY); if (name) LUKS2_activate), v2.7.1 src/utils_luks.c, man common_options.adoc (--link-vk-to-keyring with --test-passphrase)
